Petition under Section 166 & 140 of M.V. Act, 1988 for grant of compensation Award
1.

The present claim petition arises out of the Detailed Accident Report (DAR as per directions of the Hon'ble High Court of Delhi in Rajesh Tyagi Vs. Jaibir Singh; II(2010) ACC 781) filed by the Investigating Officer upon which a reasoned response has been filed by all the respondents and the same has been taken up for determination of just and reasonable compensation payable to the petitioner/injured aged 25 years who is stated to have sustained grievous injuries in the road accident in question.

sentences.text: The petitioner has filed the present claim petition U/s 166/140 M.V Act, seeking compensation to the tune of Rs. 20,00,000/- alongwith interest @ 18% p.a. from the date of filing of the present claim petition till its realization, for the injuries suffered by him in a Motor Vehicular Accident which occurred on 08.04.2019 at about 2:15 pm near Toll Tax, Village Lampur, Delhi, involving vehicle bearing registration no. HR46D-0118 (offending vehicle) which was being driven by its driver/respondent no.1 in a rash and negligent manner.

3. The concise material facts relevant to decide the present claim petition as averred are that on 08.04.2019, the petitioner/injured alongwith his cousin brother was coming from Narela to their house on vehicle bearing registration no. HR-10TMP-6983, which was being driven by the petitioner at that time.

At about 2:15 PM, when they reached near MCD Toll Tax, Village Lampur,
Delhi, offending vehicle which was being driven by its driver/respondent no.1 at a very high speed in a rash and negligent manner, came from the side of Lampur Border, suddenly turned his vehicle towards the petitioner and hit against the aforesaid vehicle of petitioner from the front side, as a result of which, both the riders of petitioner's vehicle fell down on the road and sustained injuries.
Thereafter, they were taken to SRHC Hospital, Narela, Delhi, where they were medically examined and further referred to FIMS Hospital, Bahalgarh Road, District Sonepat, Haryana.

It is categorically averred that the accident in question has taken place due to rash and negligent driving of offending vehicle bearing registration no.
MACP No. 691/19; FIR No. 128/19.; PS. Narela DOD: 15.05.2024 HR46D-0118 being driven by its driver (respondent no. 1 herein).

sentences.text: The offending vehicle was found to be possessed by respondent no. 2, owned by respondent no. 2 and insured with respondent no. 4 as on the date of accident in question.

4. In their joint written statement, the respondent no. 1 & 2 i.e. driver and registered owner have raised preliminary objections that alleged accident was not caused by the alleged offending vehicle or by the rash and negligent driving of respondent no. 1.
It has been claimed that respondent no. 1 was having valid driving licence at the time of accident.
It has been further claimed that offending vehicle was insured with respondent no. 4 at the time of accident.
On merits, they denied the averments made in the claim petition and prayed for its dismissal.

5. The insurance company had filed its legal offer, whereby it offered to pay a sum of Rs. 78,000/- as compensation towards full and final satisfaction for the claim raised by petitioner for the injuries suffered by him in the accident in question.
However, the said offer was not acceptable to the petitioner in the present case.

Accordingly, the claim petition filed by the petitioner has been proceeded further for trial for ascertainment of the just and proper compensation, that may be granted in favour of the petitioner for the injuries suffered by him in the unfortunate road accident in question.
MACP No. 691/19; FIR No. 128/19.; PS. Narela DOD: 15.05.2024 6.

sentences.text: The presence of complainant at the spot of accident at the time of accident can be substantiated by seeing the list of witnesses annexed alongwith the chargesheet filed in the criminal case wherein name of complainant Sh. Prashant is mentioned at S.No. 1.
On the other hand, respondents no. 1 & 2 have not examined any witness in order to rebut the testimony of PW1 during the course of inquiry.
Hence, there is no reason to disbelieve his uncontroverted testimony on the point of accident in question being caused by respondent no. 1 while driving the offending vehicle.
The contents of said FIR would show that the complainant has disclosed therein the same sequence of facts leading to the accident as deposed by PW1 in his evidence.
Hence, there is no possibility of any false implication of driver of offending vehicle or false involvement of the said vehicle in this case.
Furthermore, said FIR is shown to have been registered on the date of accident itself i.e. 08.04.2019.
Thus, there is no possibility of false implication of respondent no. 1 and / or false involvement of offending vehicle at the instance of the petitioner.
On the other hand, none of the respondents examined any witness in order to rebut the testimony of PW1 during the course of inquiry.

Hence, there is no reason to disbelieve his uncontroverted testimony on the point of accident in question being caused by respondent no. 1 while driving the offending vehicle in a rash and negligent manner.

The facts of the case, arguments of the Ld. Counsels, evidence, material on record and duly verified documents of the criminal case, have been carefully examined and scrutinized.

Respondent no. 1 namely Subhash Chander has been charge sheeted for offences punishable U/s. 279/337/338 IPC by the investigating agency after arriving at the conclusion on the basis of investigation carried out by it that the accident in question has taken place due to rash and negligent driving of offending vehicle.

14. It is pertinent to note that the respondent no.1/driver of offending vehicle was the other material witness to throw light by testifying as to how and under what circumstances, the accident has taken place.
However, he has preferred not to enter into the witness box.

Thus, an adverse inference is liable to be drawn against him to the effect that the accident in question has taken place due to rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle by the respondent no. 1.
There is nothing on record to show that the petitioners had any enmity with the driver of the offending vehicle so as to falsely implicate him in this case.

sentences.text: In view of the aforesaid discussion and the evidence which has come on record, it is held that the petitioner has been able to prove his case on the basis of preponderence of probabilities, that he sustained grievous injuries in road accident which took place on 08.04.2019 at about 2:15 pm near Toll Tax, Village Lampur, Delhi, due to rash and negligent driving of offending vehicle by respondent no. 1.
Thus, issue no. 1 is decided accordingly.

17. Section 168 of the Motor Vehicle Act 1988 enjoins upon the Claims Tribunal to hold an inquiry into the claim to make an award determining the amount of compensation which appears to it to be just and reasonable.

18. The intent and objective of the Beneficial Legislation is to grant equitable compensation to the vulnerable victims of road accidents and dynamic law has evolved towards grant of just and fair quantum of awards and has brought consistency and uniformity towards the desired goal.
The MACP No. 691/19; FIR No. 128/19.; PS. Narela DOD: 15.05.2024 Hon'ble Apex Court in "Sarla Verma v. Delhi Transport Corporation"

entities.text: Sarla Verma v. Delhi Transport Corporation
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: (2009) 6 SCC 121, which was affirmed by a bench of three Honble Judges in Reshma Kumari & Ors. Vs. Madan Mohan & Anr., (2013) 9 SCC 65, held as under:

entities.text: Reshma Kumari & Ors. Vs. Madan Mohan & Anr., (2013) 9 SCC 65
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: "16. "Just compensation" is adequate compensation which is fair and equitable, on the facts and circumstances of the case, to make good the loss suffered as a result of the wrong, as far as money can do so, by applying the well settled principles relating to award of compensation.
It is not intended to be a bonanza, largesse or source of profit.
17. Assessment of compensation though involving certain hypothetical considerations, should nevertheless be objective.
Justice and justness emanate from equality in treatment, consistency and thoroughness in adjudication, and fairness and uniformity in the decision making process and the decisions.
While it may not be possible to have mathematical precision or identical awards, in assessing compensation, same or similar facts should lead to awards in the same range.

When the factors/inputs are the same, and the formula/legal principles are the same,
consistency and uniformity, and not divergence and freakiness, should be the result of adjudication to arrive at just compensation..."
19.

These guiding principles for assessment of "just and reasonable compensation" have been torch bearer in injury cases also as laid down by Hon'ble Delhi High Court, in III (2007), ACC 676 titled as Oriental Insurance Co,. Ltd., Vs. Vijay Kumar Mittal & Ors, wherein it has been held:-
MACP No. 691/19; FIR No. 128/19.; PS. Narela DOD: 15.05.2024 "10.

sentences.text: The possession of one's own body is the first and most valuable all human rights and while awarding compensation for bodily injuries this primary element is to be kept in mind.
Bodily injury is to be treated and varies on account of gravity of bodily injury.

Though it is impossible to equate money with human suffering, agony and personal deprivation,

Regard must be given to the gravity and degree of deprivation as well as the degree of awareness of the deprivation.
Damages awarded in personal injury cases must be substantial and not token damages....."

11. The general principle which should govern the assessment of damages in persons injury cases is that the Court should award to injured persons such a sum as will put him in the same position as he would have been in the same position as he would have been in if he had not sustained injuries".
20.

The Hon'ble Apex Court, in further development of the legal position for grant of reasonable and fair compensation, has pronounced guiding parameters that "the compensation should be just and is not expected to be a windfall or a bonanza nor it should be niggardly or a pittance".
Reliance is placed on 2012 (8) SLT 676 titled K. Suresh Vs. New India Assurance Co. Ltd.

MACP No. 691/19; FIR No. 128/19.; PS. Narela DOD: 15.05.2024 ".....

sentences.text: The Tribunal and the Courts have to bear in mind that the basic principle lies in pragmatic computation which is in proximity to reality.
It is a well expected norm that money can not substitute a life lost but an effort has to be made for grant of just compensation having uniformity of approach.

There has to be a balance between the two extremes, that is, a windfall and the pittance, a bonanza and the modicum....."
21.
Accordingly, the entitlement of petitioner to just compensation is being assessed in the background of well settled parameters and guidelines as discussed herein-above.
MEDICAL EXPENSES 22.

Petitioner has deposed in his evidence by way of affidavit (Ex. PW1/A) that after the accident, he was taken to SRHC Hospital, Narela, Delhi, where he was medically examined and thereafter, he was referred to to FIMS Hospital, Bahalgarh Road, District Sonepat, Haryana.
He further deposed that petitioner was still under treatment.
He deposed that on 29.10.2021, he was admitted in FIMS Hospital for the purpose of removal of fixation devices and discharged on 30.10.2021.

He further deposed that the petitioner had already spent about Rs. 6,50,000/- on his medical treatment,
medicines, special diet, conveyance, attendant charges etc and was still under treatment.
During his cross-examination on behalf of insurance company
, he deposed that he had incurred medical expenses @ Rs. 3.5 - 4 lakhs in the MACP No. 691/19; FIR No. 128/19.; PS. Narela DOD: 15.05.2024 accident, which was borne by his Chacha Ji.
He denied the suggestion that he had taken medi-claim policy.

sentences.text: As already considered, the petitioner required treatment for a period of about nine months from the date of accident and remained incapacitated to resume his work of earnings for at least a period of nine months owing to grievous injuries suffered in the road traffic accident.

Apart from this, the petitioner is also shown to have sustained permanent disability to the extent of 10% in relation to his right lower limb and left upper limb and his case was right 2nd toe amputation distal phalanx with left hand deformity.

Thus, he would have undergone great physical sufferings, MACP No. 691/19;
FIR No. 128/19.; PS. Narela DOD: 15.05.2024 inconvenience and mental trauma on account of the accident in question.

Keeping in view the nature of injuries, duration of treatment and permanent disability suffered by him, a sum of Rs. 70,000/- is considered reasonable towards pain &
sufferings.
LOSS OF GENERAL AMENITIES & ENJOYMENT OF LIFE 30.
As already mentioned above, there is sufficient evidence on record to establish that the petitioner had sustained grievous injuries in the accident.

Apart from this, the petitioner is also shown to have sustained permanent disability to the extent of 10% in relation to his right lower limb and left upper limb and his case was right 2 nd toe amputation distal phalanx with left hand deformity.
Thus, he would not be able to enjoy general amenities of life after the accident in question and his quality of life has been definitely affected.

In view of the nature of injuries including permanent disability suffered by him and his continued treatment for a considerable period, I award a notional sum of Rs. 50,000/- towards loss of general amenities and enjoyment of life to the petitioner.
CONVEYANCE, SPECIAL DIET & ATTENDANT CHARGES 31.
During course of arguments, Ld. Counsel for petitioner argued that petitioner has spent considerable amount on special diet, conveyance and attendant charges.
The petitioner has failed to lead any cogent evidence on MACP No. 691/19; FIR No. 128/19.; PS. Narela DOD: 15.05.2024 record in respect of amount incurred by him under the aforesaid heads.
At the same time, it cannot be overlooked that he had sustained grievous injuries in the accident in question.
